# Wave 1 (singleton code wave): CR, behaviour-change repair, SR, CR, fold

Transcript lines already recorded:
```
wave 1 base 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
```
`REPORT_DIR=/tmp/reports`. Task 1 stays `in_progress`.

## 1. Initial CR (wave-bound, reviews the integrated worktree)

Stage all deliverables, then record the CR tree for wave 1. Run the fix-delta block with `FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'`.

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
# fix-delta-tree-shell block with FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'  -> prints <T_CR1>
```
Transcript: `wave 1 review 1 tree <T_CR1>` (CR, keyed by wave).

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "code-reviewer", output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: CODE_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md; anchors: [\"### Task 1:\"]; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md; BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111; HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: [\"node --test tests/parse.test.mjs\"]" }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["FIX_FIRST", "REJECT"] } }] })
```
Observed: `wave 1 task 1 verdict FIX_FIRST report /tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md patch n/a`.

The JSON has `behaviourChange: true`, so this triggers the reroute: fix, then SR first, then CR. `touchedTasks: [1]` means the owner is Task 1. This is review 1, so fix 1 is dispatched.

## 2. Repair (in-place, one-step carrier)

The repair worker is a plain in-place implementer in the branch checkout. It gets no worktree and no nested wave. Its payload carries no commit or staging instruction.

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "implementer", output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-fix1.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: IMPLEMENTER_STATUS_SCHEMA,
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md; anchor: ### Task 1:; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md; Work from: /workspace/project; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: [\"node --test tests/parse.test.mjs\"].\n## Previous review report (re-review trigger)\n/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md - read it yourself before repairing." }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED", "NEEDS_CONTEXT", "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS"] } }] })
```
Observed: `wave 1 task 1 status DONE report /tmp/reports/wave1-fix1.md patch n/a`.

The worker committed `2222…`, so HEAD moved. This does not change `WAVE_BASE_SHA`, which stays `1111…`. The fix delta is tree-based, so the worker commit and staging state do not affect it. The step-7 `reset --soft` will fold that commit.

Scoped gate rerun (observed passing):
```bash
(cd "/workspace/project" && node --test tests/parse.test.mjs) >"/tmp/reports/gate-0.log" 2>&1
```
The command array stays exactly as the manifest gives it. `tests/error.test.mjs` is not added to the array.

## 3. SR first: behaviour-change reroute against the integrated checkout

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A        # stages src/parse.mjs change + new tests/error.test.mjs
# fix-delta-tree-shell with FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'  -> prints <T_SR2>
git -C /workspace/project diff --stat <T_CR1> <T_SR2>   # emptiness check only
```
Transcript: `wave 1 review 2 tree <T_SR2>` (SR, keyed by Task 1).

- This SR has no previous-report marker, so it emits no `TRAJECTORY:` line.
- It still carries the `## Fix delta` block.
- Its ordinal continues Task 1's SR count. Initial SR was review 1, so this is SR review 2.

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "spec-reviewer", output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-sr2.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: SPEC_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      acceptance: { level: "none", reason: "the parent takes the SR verdict from structured JSON; review tree is staged by design" },
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md; anchor: ### Task 1:; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md. Review the integrated checkout /workspace/project; repair report: /tmp/reports/wave1-fix1.md; read it yourself; never run tests.\n## Fix delta\ntree-before: <T_CR1>\ntree-after: <T_SR2>\nRun git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <T_CR1> <T_SR2> yourself." }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["NEEDS_REWORK", "OUT_OF_SCOPE_CHANGES"] } }] })
```
Observed: `wave 1 task 1 verdict COMPLIANT report /tmp/reports/wave1-sr2.md patch n/a`.

## 4. CR re-review (round 2)

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
# fix-delta-tree-shell with FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'  -> prints <T_CR2>
git -C /workspace/project diff --stat <T_CR1> <T_CR2>
```
Transcript: `wave 1 review 2 tree <T_CR2>` (CR, keyed by wave).

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "code-reviewer", output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-cr2.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: CODE_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md; anchors: [\"### Task 1:\"]; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md; BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111; HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: [\"node --test tests/parse.test.mjs\"].\n## Previous review report (re-review trigger)\n/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md - read it yourself; apply the trajectory block from code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md (TRAJECTORY line only if issues remain).\n## Fix delta\ntree-before: <T_CR1>\ntree-after: <T_CR2>\nRun git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <T_CR1> <T_CR2> yourself." }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["FIX_FIRST", "REJECT"] } }] })
```
`HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE` against base `1111…` covers both the worker commit `2222…` and the staged changes.

Observed: `wave 1 task 1 verdict SHIP report /tmp/reports/wave1-cr2.md patch n/a`. This is a clean review, so the loop ends.

## 5. Fold, commit, complete (only after SR COMPLIANT and CR SHIP)

```bash
git -C /workspace/project reset --soft 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 \
 && git -C /workspace/project add -A \
 && git -C /workspace/project commit -m "Task 1: parse numbers (reject empty strings)"
git -C /workspace/project status --porcelain   # expect clean
git -C /workspace/project rev-parse HEAD       # next wave's WAVE_BASE_SHA
```
- The `reset --soft` folds `2222…` and all staged changes into one durable wave commit whose parent is `1111…`.
- An empty commit would mean stop; Task 1 would not be completed.

Then mark the task complete:
```ts
plan_tracker({ action: "update", index: <Task 1 index>, status: "complete" })
```
After that, execute any explicit manifest `orchestrator` instruction for Task 1 once, before the next wave.

## Empty repair delta

An empty delta means `diff --stat <T_CR1> <T_SR2>` prints nothing. That covers both no change at all and ignored-only edits. It means the fix changed no tracked file, even if HEAD moved, because an empty commit or a commit identical to the tree changes nothing.

In that case:
- Dispatch no SR and no CR re-review.
- Count it as a failed attempt under When a Subagent Fails.
- Re-dispatch the in-place implementer with `/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md` and the note "your fix changed no tracked file".
- After two failed attempts, stop: escalate under amend permission, or report. Task 1 stays `in_progress`.

The following are proposed commands and dispatches, not executed actions. Schema names refer to the supplied dispatch-contract schemas.

### 1. Initial integrated-wave CR

Keep the wave base fixed even if a repair later commits:

```text
wave 1 base 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
```

Stage deliverables and capture the review tree using the prescribed scratch-index recipe:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A

FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
FD_STATUS=$?
rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"
```

Retain the printed object ID as `T0`; stop on capture failure. Record:

```text
wave 1 review 1 tree /workspace/project
```

```js
subagent({
  async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{
    parallel: [{
      agent: "code-reviewer",
      output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: CODE_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      task: `planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md
anchor: "### Task 1:"
Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md
Spec anchors: lines 8-10
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: ["node --test tests/parse.test.mjs"]
Review the integrated staged and unstaged wave diff, including new files.
Read the anchored task, spec, Tests contract and applicable Rules yourself.
Use the supplied code-quality reviewer template and report contract,
including behaviourChange. Do not edit files.`
    }],
    stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["FIX_FIRST", "REJECT"] }
  }]
})
```

Consume the supplied JSON, including `behaviourChange: true` and `touchedTasks: [1]`:

```text
wave 1 task 1 verdict FIX_FIRST report /tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md
```

No patch path was supplied for this in-place review.

### 2. Repair in the integrated checkout

Do not create a nested worktree or instruct the worker to commit.

```js
subagent({
  async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{
    parallel: [{
      agent: "implementer",
      output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-fix1.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: IMPLEMENTER_STATUS_SCHEMA,
      task: `planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md
anchor: "### Task 1:"
Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md
Spec anchors: lines 8-10
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: ["node --test tests/parse.test.mjs"]
Read the anchored task, Tests contract, spec and applicable Rules.
Repair the integrated checkout in place.
## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md
Read that report yourself; verify and resolve its findings.
Return DONE, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, NEEDS_CONTEXT or BLOCKED explicitly,
with test-contract evidence and schema-matching structured output.`
    }],
    stopOn: {
      path: "/status",
      in: ["BLOCKED", "NEEDS_CONTEXT", "DONE_WITH_CONCERNS"]
    }
  }]
})
```

Supplied observation:

```text
wave 1 task 1 status DONE report /tmp/reports/wave1-fix1.md
```

The worker reports `COMMITTED` at `2222222222222222222222222222222222222222`. Preserve the original wave base.

Rerun the scoped gate:

```bash
(cd "/workspace/project" && node --test tests/parse.test.mjs) >"/tmp/reports/gate-repair-1.log" 2>&1
```

After the supplied passing result, run `git add -A` and repeat the **entire scratch-index capture block above**. Retain its printed object ID as `T1`.

```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --stat <T0> <T1>
```

`T0` and `T1` mean the actual captured tree IDs, not commit SHAs.

### 3. Behavior-changing repair: SR first, then CR

```text
wave 1 review 2 tree /workspace/project
```

Dispatch a one-step SR carrier, with `async: false`, `context: "fresh"`, `cwd: "/workspace/project"`, and:

```js
chain: [{
  parallel: [{
    agent: "spec-reviewer",
    output: "/tmp/reports/wave1-sr2.md",
    outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: SPEC_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
    task: `planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/numbers.md
anchor: "### Task 1:"
Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md
Spec anchors: lines 8-10
Implementer report: /tmp/reports/wave1-fix1.md
Read anchored requirements and Rules; never run tests.
Review the behavior-changing repair against the spec.
## Fix delta
tree-before: <T0>
tree-after: <T1>
FD_ROOT: /workspace/project
Run git -C "/workspace/project" diff --binary <T0> <T1>
and read the repair-only delta.`
  }],
  stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["NEEDS_REWORK", "OUT_OF_SCOPE_CHANGES"] }
}]
```

This rerouted SR is a first review of the repair: **no previous-review marker**.

Supplied observation:

```text
wave 1 task 1 verdict COMPLIANT report /tmp/reports/wave1-sr2.md
```

Stage and capture again before CR; record its actual tree as `T2`.

```text
wave 1 review 2 tree /workspace/project
```

Dispatch the initial CR carrier again as a **one-step re-review**, changing output to `/tmp/reports/wave1-cr2.md`; retain base, `WORKTREE`, anchors, schema, scoped commands and stopOn. Add:

```text
SR report: /tmp/reports/wave1-sr2.md
## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
/tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md
Read the prior report yourself.
## Fix delta
tree-before: <T0>
tree-after: <T2>
Run git -C "/workspace/project" diff --binary <T0> <T2>.
If issues remain, emit structured trajectory and the prescribed TRAJECTORY
line: STAGNANT for materially unchanged prior blocking findings;
otherwise DIVERGING for nondecreasing blocking count or new blocking findings;
otherwise CONVERGING with counts and maximum severity.
If clean, omit trajectory.
```

Supplied observation:

```text
wave 1 task 1 verdict SHIP report /tmp/reports/wave1-cr2.md
```

### 4. Fold only after acceptance

```bash
git -C /workspace/project reset --soft 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 &&
git -C /workspace/project add -A &&
git -C /workspace/project commit -m "fix: validate numeric input"
```

Only after successful nonempty commit:

```js
plan_tracker({ action: "update", index: 1, status: "complete" })
```

Use the existing tracker’s positional index for Task 1 if it differs.

An empty repair delta means no tracked repair occurred—even if HEAD moved. Dispatch no re-review; count a failed attempt and resend the prior report to a fresh repair worker with “your fix changed no tracked file,” respecting the two-attempt limit.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved: After keeps BASE_SHA 1111/HEAD_SHA WORKTREE through both CRs after the worker's 2222 commit, computes the repair-only delta from scratch-index tree captures (T_CR1 -> T_SR2/T_CR2) with diff --binary and treats an empty delta as a failed attempt with no re-review, dispatches one in-place one-step implementer with no commit/staging text, routes SR against /workspace/project before CR, folds via reset --soft/add -A/commit only after COMPLIANT+SHIP, and now prints explicit `wave N task N verdict/status ... report ... patch` and `review N tree` transcript lines, which is an improvement over Before's prose-only observations. Two soft points worth tightening so repair-review-root does not drift in other cases: After's SR payload dropped Before's explicit 'read its Tests: block and Test: paths as contract' instruction (it supplies only planPath/anchor/Spec), and it points the SR at the fix report rather than the prior CR report; keep the anchor-based Tests-contract phrase and name the prior review report path alongside the Fix delta. Also the added `acceptance: { level: "none" }` on the SR item is outside the stated facts but is unusual for a chain whose acceptance is already chain-only; either drop it or justify it against the SR chain-only acceptance override so it is not read as a funding/gate change.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept and additionally repairs delegation-boundary: Before declared SR "schema-free" with a non-verdict stop and insisted the CR re-review must embed the complete previous report verbatim (declaring a path-only reference inadequate), both of which break the one-step schema-bound/stopOn chain and the no-pasted-report rule; After binds SR to SPEC_VERDICT_SCHEMA with a verdict stopOn and passes /tmp/reports/wave1-cr1.md by path under the re-review marker. Two soft spots to tighten without losing anything: (1) the primary only runs `git diff --stat <T0> <T1>` and delegates the `--binary` diff to the reviewer; have the primary itself run `git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <T0> <T1> > /tmp/reports/wave1-fix1.delta.patch`, check it is nonempty (that is the empty-delta failed-attempt check), and print the patch path as the 'patch' observation, then pass that path under `## Fix delta`; (2) name the Tests contract explicitly in the SR payload (as the CR and repair payloads do) and drop the `## Previous review report (re-review trigger)` heading from the implementer payload, using a plain `Prior findings: <path>` line, so the re-review marker stays reserved for reviewer re-dispatches.
